_comment: Category-level starting points in GBP. Used by build_dashboard.py for Tab 5 and for CPL colouring. Override per run with the 'benchmarks' key in the input file.

Google.best_for: High-intent search and broad display reach
Google.note: Search captures existing demand and is usually the highest-volume channel. Display and remarketing inflate volume but lower lead quality. Expect CPL to rise with brand-term competition.

Meta.best_for: Consumer and SMB demand generation, retargeting
Meta.note: Creative drives results. Lead-form campaigns give cheap leads of lower intent. Frequent creative refresh is needed to hold CPL.

LinkedIn.best_for: B2B targeting by job title, seniority and company
LinkedIn.note: Highest CPL of the eight channels but the strongest firmographic targeting. Best for ABM and enterprise offers.

TikTok.note: Cheap reach and leads, but intent is lower. Native-looking creative outperforms polished ads.

Bing.best_for: Search with an older, desktop-heavy, higher-income skew
Bing.note: Lower volume than Google but often lower CPC. Competitors frequently under-invest here, so it is a cheap place to copy proven Google structure.

YouTube.note: Works best as a mid-funnel and remarketing channel. Direct-response CPL is higher than search.

Reddit.best_for: Niche communities and technical or enthusiast audiences
Reddit.note: Low competition and cheap clicks, but needs community-native tone. A good first-mover test channel.

DSP.best_for: Programmatic reach, CTV and audience extension
DSP.note: Useful for scale and remarketing across the open web. Attribution is weaker, so judge on assisted conversions.
